title: Dynamic Alerting Platform — Tenant Configuration Schema
description: JSON Schema (draft-07) for validating tenant YAML configuration files in conf.d/. Supports threshold customization, alert routing, maintenance windows, and metadata injection.
$comment: Applies to conf.d tenant files, flat or nested: extension .yaml or .yml in any case, basename NOT starting with `_` or `.` (the set scripts/tools/lint/check_confd_schema.py validates). Editor binding: copy the yaml.schemas block from .devcontainer/devcontainer.json (not repeated here; see docs/internal/editor-schema-validation.md for why the globs look the way they do).

tenants.title: Tenant Configuration Map
tenants.description: Mapping of tenant-id (string) to per-tenant configuration (object). Each tenant can define thresholds, routing, metadata, and operational modes.

tenantId.description: Tenant id (ADR-035): a DNS-1123 label — 1-63 characters of lowercase letters, digits and '-', starting and ending with a letter or digit.
tenantId.$comment: The one authored copy of the tenant-id rule (ADR-035 D2). Go (pkg/tenantid/tenant_id.json) and the portal (_common/data/tenant-id.json) read copies generated by scripts/tools/dx/gen_tenant_id_json.py; Python reads this definition at runtime (_lib_validation.tenant_id_rule). The pattern may only use the subset ECMA-262, Python re and Go RE2 agree on; match it as a full match.

duration.title: Alertmanager duration
duration.description: A duration as Alertmanager reads it: whole numbers with units, largest unit first, each unit at most once — y (365d), w, d, h, m, s, ms — or a bare 0. Examples: 30s, 5m, 1h30m, 1d. Not accepted: fractions (1.5h), units out of order (30m1h) or repeated (1h1h), ns / us / µs, signs, spaces.
duration.$comment: #2490: the one authored copy of the routing timing syntax. Source: prometheus/common v0.67.5 (the version in components/threshold-exporter/app/go.mod) model.ParseDuration, which Alertmanager's config loader runs on every group_wait / group_interval / repeat_interval. That version parses by hand; this pattern is its equivalent and is word for word the durationRE of earlier prometheus/common releases (v0.32.1: "^(([0-9]+)y)?(([0-9]+)w)?(([0-9]+)d)?(([0-9]+)h)?(([0-9]+)m)?(([0-9]+)s)?(([0-9]+)ms)?$") with ParseDuration's two special cases folded in: "0" is accepted without a unit and "" is refused (minLength). `not` covers jsonschema's re.search letting `$` match before a final newline. ⚠️ Not expressible here: ParseDuration also refuses a value that overflows int64 nanoseconds (about 292y, e.g. 293y or 1000000000000h, "duration out of range"); the route generator's parser (_lib_validation.am_duration_seconds, which reads this definition) and the exporter (model.ParseDuration itself) refuse it. tests/shared/am_duration_matrix.json holds Go's verdicts; tests/shared/test_am_duration_parity.py holds this pattern and the Python parser to them. Uses only the regex subset ECMA-262, Python re and Go RE2 agree on.

propertyNames.$comment: GENERATED by scripts/tools/dx/sync_schema.py --update from components/threshold-exporter/app/pkg/config/reserved_keys.json — DO NOT EDIT. Closes the `_` namespace (#3016 R3): a `_`-prefixed key is either one the platform reads, or a typo nothing reads.
propertyNames.patternErrorMessage: A key starting with '_' must be one the platform reads: _custom_alerts, _metadata, _namespaces, _profile, _routing, _routing_profile, _severity_dedup, _silent_mode, _state_<name>. Any other '_' key is read by nothing.

tenantConfig.title: Per-Tenant Configuration
tenantConfig.description: Configuration for a single tenant. Supports metric thresholds (from Rule Packs), operational modes (_state_*, _silent_mode), routing, metadata, and scheduled overrides.

_profile.title: Profile Reference (v1.12.0)
_profile.description: Reference to a profile name defined in _profiles.yaml. Profile values act as fill-in (not overwrite) — tenant settings take precedence. Inheritance chain: _defaults.yaml → profile → tenant config. A profile's `_severity_dedup` and `_routing*` keys are not filled in (#2914; docs/cli-reference.md#guard, routing_in_unread_location).

_metadata.title: Tenant Metadata
_metadata.description: Optional metadata fields injected into all alert annotations. Exposed as tenant_metadata_info{tenant, runbook_url, owner, tier} = 1 metric. Supports {{tenant}} placeholder in runbook_url.

_silent_mode.title: Silent Mode Configuration
_silent_mode.description: Suppress Alertmanager notifications while keeping TSDB records. Alerts still fire and are recorded, but notifications are blocked. Useful for transient noisy alerts during known issues.

_state_maintenance.title: Maintenance Mode Configuration
_state_maintenance.description: Suppress alerts at PromQL level (no TSDB records). Useful for planned maintenance windows. Supports one-time expiry and recurring schedules (v1.11.0). Distinct from silent_mode.

_severity_dedup.title: Severity Deduplication Mode
_severity_dedup.description: Controls Alertmanager inhibition behavior for multi-severity alerts: 'enable' (default — suppress the warning notification when critical fires for the same tenant + metric_group) or 'disable' (receive both notifications). See definitions.severityDedup for every spelling read, and docs/design/config-driven.md §2.8.

_namespaces.title: Kubernetes Namespaces (N:1 Tenant Mapping)
_namespaces.description: List of Kubernetes namespaces this tenant maps to. Used by scaffold_tenant.py and da-tools N:1 mapping tooling (v1.8.0+). See architecture-and-design.md §2.3.

_routing_profile.title: Routing Profile Reference (v2.1.0 ADR-007)
_routing_profile.description: Reference to a named routing profile defined in _routing_profiles.yaml. Profile values act as Layer 2 in the four-layer merge: _routing_defaults → routing_profiles[ref] → tenant _routing → _routing_enforced. Tenant _routing keys override profile values.

oneOf.description: Turns this tenant's routing off: disable / disabled / off / false, case-insensitive, surrounding whitespace ignored (the set _lib_validation.is_disabled accepts). Must be a YAML string: an unquoted off / false is a boolean, which the route generator refuses (#2341) — quote it ('off').

_routing.title: Alert Routing Configuration
_routing.description: Per-tenant alert routing to custom receivers (webhook, email, slack, teams, rocketchat, pagerduty). Supports per-alertname and metric_group overrides. Tenant routing is inserted after _routing_enforced. A disabling string turns the tenant's routing off; any other non-mapping value is refused (#2341).

_custom_alerts.title: Custom Alerts (v2.9.0 ADR-024 Capability B)
_custom_alerts.description: Tenant-authored declarative custom alerts via platform recipes. Declared here (tenant leaf) they apply only to this tenant and replace, whole, the list of the profile it binds (no merge; ADR-024 §3). Compiled to ONE vectorized rule per shape (rule count = shape count, not per-tenant fan-out). Tenants never write PromQL.

^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*\\{.*\\}$.title: Dimensional Threshold
^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*\\{.*\\}$.description: Metric with dimensional labels: metric{label="value"} or metric{label=~"regex"}. Labels can be literal (=) or regex (=~). Examples: redis_queue_length{queue="orders"}, mysql_connections{schema=~"temp.*"}

thresholdScalar.title: Threshold Value (Scalar)
thresholdScalar.description: Simple string threshold. Values: numeric threshold (e.g., '70'), 'disable' (stop alerting), or 'value:severity' (e.g., '1000:critical'). The severity after the LAST ':' must be warning or critical, in any letter case; any other suffix ('70:high', the empty '70:') makes the value unreadable, and the exporter serves it like an unparseable value (#3071; the pattern below checks the suffix only, tests/shared/threshold_value_matrix.json pins it to the exporter). Three-state design: custom value, omit (use default), or 'disable' — the 'omit' state applies only to keys that have a value under 'defaults:' in _defaults.yaml. A key the platform only DECLARES (its 'optional_overrides:' list) has no default to inherit, so omitting it means no value and no series at all.
thresholdScalar.patternErrorMessage: The severity after the last ':' must be warning or critical (any letter case), e.g. '70:critical'; any other suffix, such as '70:high' or the empty '70:', makes the whole value unreadable and the exporter serves the platform default instead (#3071).

scheduledValue.title: Scheduled Threshold with Time-Window Overrides
scheduledValue.description: Structured threshold with default and optional time-window overrides (v1.11.0 B4). Allows different thresholds at different UTC times. Supports cross-midnight windows (e.g., 22:00-06:00). See architecture-and-design.md §2.5.

default.title: Default Threshold Value
default.description: Default threshold applied outside any override window.

overrides.title: Time-Window Overrides
overrides.description: List of UTC time windows with override values. First matching window wins. Matched as HH:MM-HH:MM (24-hour format, UTC-only). Supports cross-midnight (e.g., 22:00-06:00 = 10PM to 6AM).

expires.title: Override Expiry (time-boxed threshold, PREVENT #656)
expires.description: ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 instant after which this override auto-reverts to the platform default (fail-safe: more protection, never silent) and emits da_config_event{event="threshold_expired"} to trigger a cleanup PR. v1: honored only on base standard metrics (those in _defaults.yaml); ignored on dimensional / _critical / custom-alert keys. On expiry it reverts to whatever platform default is in effect AT THAT TIME (the SSOT baseline) — which may be tighter than the default when this expires was set, if the platform default changed in between.

reason.title: Expiry Reason
reason.description: Human-readable reason for the time-boxed override (e.g. the incident it mitigates). Surfaced in da_config_event on expiry.

timeWindowOverride.title: Time-Window Override
timeWindowOverride.description: Override threshold value for a specific UTC time window (HH:MM-HH:MM format, 24-hour).

window.title: UTC Time Window
window.description: Window in HH:MM-HH:MM format (24-hour, UTC-only). Example: '01:00-09:00' (1AM to 9AM). Supports cross-midnight (e.g., '22:00-06:00' = 10PM to 6AM).

value.title: Override Threshold Value
value.description: Threshold value to use within this window. Same syntax as scalar thresholds (numeric, 'disable', or 'value:severity').

metadata.title: Tenant Metadata
metadata.description: Optional metadata injected into all alerts from this tenant. Exposed as tenant_metadata_info{tenant, runbook_url, owner, tier} = 1 metric. Supports {{tenant}} placeholder.
metadata.$comment: v2.7.0 ADR-016: When files are in hierarchical conf.d/ (domain/region/env/), the directory path infers default values for domain, region, and environment. Explicit _metadata fields override path-inferred values. CI may warn when path and field disagree.

runbook_url.title: Runbook URL
runbook_url.description: Base URL to tenant-specific runbooks/documentation. Supports {{tenant}} placeholder. Example: 'https://wiki.example.com/{{tenant}}'

owner.title: Owner/Team
owner.description: Team or person responsible for this tenant's monitoring. Free-form string for annotation purposes.

tier.title: Business Tier
tier.description: Business tier/SLA level for prioritization. Examples: tier-1, tier-2, non-critical.

environment.title: Environment
environment.description: Deployment environment for RBAC filtering. Examples: production, staging, development.

region.title: Region
region.description: Geographic region or data center for this tenant.

domain.title: Business Domain
domain.description: Business domain for RBAC filtering and grouping. Examples: finance, ecommerce, infrastructure.

db_type.title: Database Type
db_type.description: Primary database type for this tenant. Used for dimension-based grouping AND (since #869) to opt the tenant into per-tenant exporter liveness: the exporter emits tenant_expected_exporter{tenant,db_type} ONLY when db_type is set — the LHS of the TenantExporterAbsent anti-join. A typo'd KEY (e.g. dbType / db_typ) is caught by this object's additionalProperties:false; a typo'd VALUE is caught by this enum. Either typo previously dropped db_type silently to "", removing the tenant from liveness with no signal (#880 Day-3 hardening).
db_type.$comment: enum SSOT = the database rule-packs in PACK_ORDER (scripts/tools/dx/generate_platform_data.py) minus the app/platform packs (jvm/nginx/kubernetes/operational/platform/custom-alerts/liveness). Extend this list when adding a new DB exporter rule-pack.

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: Free-form tags for flexible categorization and filtering.

groups.title: Groups
groups.description: Group membership references. Groups are defined in _groups.yaml.

metadata.$comment: additionalProperties:false (was true) so a mistyped _metadata KEY is rejected at author/CI time instead of being silently swallowed — this is the shift-left half of the #880 db_type-typo fix (a dbType/db_typ key no longer parses to DBType="" undetected). All legitimate metadata fields are enumerated above; add a property here before introducing a new one.

oneOf.title: Silent Mode (Scalar, Backward Compatible)
oneOf.description: Legacy scalar format: 'warning', 'critical', 'all', or 'disable'. For new configs, prefer structured format with expires/reason.

oneOf.title: Silent Mode (Structured, v1.7.0+)
oneOf.description: Structured format with optional expiry and reason. Alerts fire but Alertmanager suppresses notifications. Distinct from maintenance mode which suppresses at PromQL level.

target.title: Target Severity
target.description: Which severity levels to suppress: 'warning', 'critical', or 'all'.

expires.title: Expiration Timestamp (RFC3339)
expires.description: RFC3339 UTC timestamp (e.g. 2099-04-01T00:00:00Z). Silent mode auto-expires at this time. Optional; omit for indefinite silent mode. A value the exporter cannot parse as RFC3339 (e.g. a quoted date without time) logs a WARN and the whole _silent_mode setting is ignored: nothing is silenced (#2000, fail-closed).

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Human-readable reason for silent mode. Optional; appears in observability logs.

maintenanceMode.title: Maintenance Mode Configuration
maintenanceMode.description: Suppress alerts at PromQL level (no TSDB records). Useful for planned maintenance. Distinct from silent_mode. Accepts the scalar state-filter shorthand ('enable'/'disable', like every other _state_* filter) OR the structured object (one-time expiry / recurring schedules).
maintenanceMode.$comment: oneOf[scalar, object] mirrors silentMode. The scalar form is what the exporter actually accepts for any _state_* filter (resolve.go ResolveStateFiltersAt: any non-'disable' value enables; the structured branch is taken only when the value contains 'expires:'). Modelling it object-only previously rejected the valid scalar form at schema-validation time (#880 surfaced this on examples/redis-tenant.yaml).

oneOf.title: Maintenance State (Scalar shorthand)
oneOf.description: 'enable' = this tenant is in maintenance (its alerts are suppressed via the user_state_filter{filter="maintenance"} unless-join); 'disable' = inactive. For one-time expiry or recurring windows use the structured object form below.

oneOf.title: Maintenance Mode (Structured)
oneOf.description: Structured form with optional one-time expiry and recurring schedules (cron).

target.title: Target
target.description: Status: 'enable' (default) or 'disable'. When 'disable', maintenance mode is inactive.

enabled.title: Enabled Flag
enabled.description: Boolean equivalent of target field. true = 'enable', false = 'disable'. Use either 'target' (string) or 'enabled' (boolean).

expires.title: Expiration Timestamp (RFC3339)
expires.description: RFC3339 UTC timestamp (e.g. 2099-04-01T00:00:00Z). Maintenance mode auto-expires at this time. Optional; omit for indefinite maintenance. A value the exporter cannot parse as RFC3339 (e.g. a quoted date without time) logs a WARN and the whole _state_maintenance setting is ignored: maintenance is not active (#2000, fail-closed).

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Human-readable reason for maintenance. Optional; appears in observability logs.

recurring.title: Recurring Maintenance Windows (v1.11.0+)
recurring.description: List of periodic maintenance schedules (e.g., weekly backups). Processed by maintenance_scheduler.py CronJob to auto-generate Alertmanager silences.

recurringSchedule.title: Recurring Schedule
recurringSchedule.description: Periodic maintenance window defined by cron expression and duration. Processed by maintenance_scheduler.py to auto-generate Alertmanager silences. See docs/architecture-and-design.md §2.7.

cron.title: Cron Expression
cron.description: Standard 5-field cron (minute hour dayOfMonth month dayOfWeek) in UTC. Examples: '0 2 * * *' (daily 2AM), '0 3 * * 0' (Sunday 3AM).

duration.title: Duration
duration.description: Go-style duration (e.g., '4h', '30m', '2h30m'). Maintenance window = cron start time + duration.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Human-readable reason for recurring maintenance. Optional.

routing.title: Alert Routing Configuration
routing.description: Per-tenant alert routing to custom receivers. Supports one primary receiver, per-alertname/metric_group overrides and label-match sub-routes (routes). Replaces _routing_defaults. Also the shape of one routing profile in _routing_profiles.yaml (routing-profiles.schema.json $refs this definition, ADR-007). See architecture-and-design.md §2.9 and cli-reference.md.
routing.$comment: #1339 P1 / #2521 — explicit null is accepted on six fields (group_by, group_wait, group_interval, repeat_interval, overrides, routes) and nowhere else in this definition. Rationale, all measured against generate_alertmanager_routes.py with identical fixtures: the routing layers (_routing_defaults → routing profile → this) merge one top-level key at a time (shallow), so a null on one of these replaces the inherited value with nothing — the timing fields and group_by are then omitted from the route, and null overrides / routes render no override / label-match sub-route, exactly like []. The generator and validate-config accept it (#2521 pinned each; da-guard no longer judges routing and tenant-api asks the generator, ADR-036). 'receiver: ~' is deliberately still rejected — it makes the tenant's ENTIRE route disappear ('WARN: missing required receiver, skipping'), so a one-character typo would silently reroute every alert for that tenant to the catch-all. ⚠️ This definition is the tenant's _routing (and a routing profile); a null in a SUBDIRECTORY level's _routing_defaults is a different thing — the generator refuses it (exit 2, routing_defaults_null_below_root), and definitions.routingDefaults keeps refusing it.

receiver.title: Primary Receiver
receiver.description: Default receiver for alerts from this tenant. Can be webhook, email, slack, teams, rocketchat, or pagerduty. Null is NOT accepted here — it would drop the tenant's whole route (see $comment).

group_by.title: Group By Labels
group_by.description: Alertmanager grouping labels (e.g., ['alertname', 'tenant']). Optional; defaults to Alertmanager config. Explicit null opts out of the inherited _routing_defaults value.

group_wait.title: Group Wait Duration
group_wait.description: Wait time before sending initial notification (duration syntax: definitions/duration, e.g. '30s'). Guardrail: 5s–5m. Explicit null opts out of the inherited value. See architecture-and-design.md §2.9.

group_interval.title: Group Interval Duration
group_interval.description: Interval between notifications for same group (duration syntax: definitions/duration, e.g. '5m'). Guardrail: 5s–5m. Explicit null opts out of the inherited value. See architecture-and-design.md §2.9.

repeat_interval.title: Repeat Interval Duration
repeat_interval.description: Interval for re-sending unresolved alerts (duration syntax: definitions/duration, e.g. '4h' or '1h30m'). Guardrail: 1m–72h. Explicit null opts out of the inherited value. See architecture-and-design.md §2.9.

overrides.title: Per-Alertname/Metric-Group Overrides
overrides.description: List of routing overrides for specific alert names or metric groups. First matching override wins. Replaces the inherited _routing_defaults / profile overrides wholesale (shallow merge). Explicit null opts out of the inherited value (same as []). See architecture-and-design.md §2.9.

routes.title: Label-Match Sub-Routes (ADR-007)
routes.description: Sub-routes selected by label equality (e.g. escalate severity=critical to PagerDuty). Rendered as children of the tenant's main route AFTER the overrides, so the order is overrides → routes → the main route's own receiver; the first matching child wins. A tenant _routing.routes replaces a routing profile's routes wholesale (shallow merge, same as overrides). Explicit null opts out of the inherited value (same as []). Not accepted in _routing_defaults.

receiver.title: Receiver Configuration
receiver.description: Alert receiver definition. Must specify 'type' and required fields based on type. See cli-reference.md for field details.

webhookReceiver.title: Webhook Receiver
webhookReceiver.description: Generic HTTP POST receiver. Sends alert to a webhook URL. Supports optional HTTP config.

url.title: Webhook URL
url.description: HTTP endpoint to POST alerts to. Subject to webhook domain allowlist policy (if configured).

send_resolved.title: Send Resolved
send_resolved.description: Whether to send alert resolved notifications. Default: true.

http_config.title: HTTP Configuration
http_config.description: Optional HTTP client settings (auth, TLS, proxy). See Alertmanager http_config docs.

emailReceiver.title: Email Receiver
emailReceiver.description: SMTP email receiver. Sends alerts via email to specified recipients.

to.title: Recipient Email Addresses
to.description: List of email addresses to send alerts to.

smarthost.title: SMTP Server
smarthost.description: SMTP server address in host:port format (numeric port; an IPv6 host is bracketed, e.g. '[2001:db8::1]:25'). Example: 'smtp.example.com:587'

from.title: From Address
from.description: Sender email address. Required: the platform configures SMTP per receiver with no global smtp_from, and Alertmanager rejects an email config without `from` unless a global smtp_from is set.

auth_password.title: SMTP Password
auth_password.description: Password for SMTP authentication. Optional. Use Kubernetes Secrets in production.

require_tls.title: Require TLS
require_tls.description: Require TLS for SMTP connection. Default: true.

html.title: HTML Template
html.description: Alertmanager template for HTML email body. Optional; uses Alertmanager default if omitted.

text.title: Text Template
text.description: Alertmanager template for the plain-text email body. Optional.

send_resolved.title: Send Resolved
send_resolved.description: Whether to send resolved notifications. Default: true.

slackReceiver.title: Slack Receiver
slackReceiver.description: Slack webhook receiver. Posts alerts to a Slack channel.

api_url.title: Slack Webhook URL
api_url.description: Slack incoming webhook URL. Create at https://api.slack.com/messaging/webhooks

channel.title: Slack Channel
channel.description: Channel to post to (optional; defaults to webhook's configured channel). Example: '#alerts' or '#my-team'

title.title: Message Title
title.description: Custom title/heading for Slack message. Alertmanager template string (e.g., '{{ .GroupLabels.alertname }}').

text.title: Message Body
text.description: Custom body text for Slack message. Alertmanager template string.

title_link.title: Title Link
title_link.description: URL the message title links to. Alertmanager template string.

icon_emoji.title: Icon Emoji
icon_emoji.description: Emoji used as the message icon (e.g., ':rotating_light:').

send_resolved.title: Send Resolved
send_resolved.description: Whether to send resolved notifications. Default: true.

teamsReceiver.title: Microsoft Teams Receiver
teamsReceiver.description: Microsoft Teams webhook receiver. Posts alerts to Teams channel.

webhook_url.title: Teams Webhook URL
webhook_url.description: Microsoft Teams incoming webhook URL. Create at https://outlook.webhook.office.com

title.title: Card Title
title.description: Custom title for Teams card. Alertmanager template string.

text.title: Card Text
text.description: Custom body text for Teams card. Alertmanager template string.

send_resolved.title: Send Resolved
send_resolved.description: Whether to send resolved notifications. Default: true.

rocketchatReceiver.title: Rocket.Chat Receiver
rocketchatReceiver.description: Rocket.Chat webhook receiver. Posts alerts to Rocket.Chat channel.

channel.title: Channel
channel.description: Channel name. Metadata field (not passed to Alertmanager).

username.title: Bot Username
username.description: Bot username for posting. Metadata field (not passed to Alertmanager).

icon_url.title: Icon URL
icon_url.description: Icon URL for bot avatar. Metadata field (not passed to Alertmanager).

send_resolved.title: Send Resolved
send_resolved.description: Whether to send resolved notifications. Default: true.

pagerdutReceiver.title: PagerDuty Receiver
pagerdutReceiver.description: PagerDuty incident receiver. Creates/resolves PagerDuty incidents. Set exactly one of service_key (Events API v1) or routing_key (Events API v2) — not both, not neither; an empty or null value counts as not set.
pagerdutReceiver.$comment: #2137: exactly one of service_key / routing_key, expressed as a oneOf of single-field branches `{required: [k], properties: {k: {type: string, minLength: 1}}}` (both set matches both branches and fails oneOf; neither matches none). Empty and null count as unset, matching Alertmanager (its config is a Go struct: "" and a YAML null — e.g. `service_key:` rendered empty by envsubst — both decode to the zero value = not given) and the Python check. Hence the key properties allow null, and each branch needs BOTH `type: string` (minLength does not apply to null, so without it a null key would satisfy the branch) and `minLength: 1`. Alertmanager accepts both keys at once but then uses the v1 API via service_key and silently ignores routing_key (notify/pagerduty/pagerduty.go), so both-set is rejected here. Python RECEIVER_TYPES (exactly_one_of) reads this same shape; its parity test (tests/shared/test_receiver_spec_parity.py) fails on any other presence keyword here.

service_key.title: Service Key (Integration Key)
service_key.description: PagerDuty service integration key for events API v1. Deprecated in favor of routing_key (v2). Mutually exclusive with routing_key.

routing_key.title: Routing Key (v2 API)
routing_key.description: PagerDuty integration key for events API v2. Recommended over service_key. Mutually exclusive with service_key.

severity.title: Severity Mapping
severity.description: PagerDuty severity level. Alertmanager template string (e.g., '{{ .Status }}'). Default: 'error'.

description.title: Incident Description
description.description: Custom incident description. Alertmanager template string.

client.title: Client Name
client.description: Monitoring tool name. Alertmanager template string (e.g., 'Prometheus').

client_url.title: Client URL
client_url.description: Link back to monitoring system. Alertmanager template string.

send_resolved.title: Send Resolved
send_resolved.description: Whether to resolve PagerDuty incidents on alert resolution. Default: true.

secretRef.title: Kubernetes Secret Reference
secretRef.description: Reference to one key of a Kubernetes Secret, in place of the credential's literal value. The Secret is created by the operator or ExternalSecrets, not by this config; the generator is to render the reference as the matching Alertmanager `*_file` field (SecretKeySelector) instead of copying the value. Not wired to any field yet: a credential field accepts this shape only once the generator renders it (#1560). Distinct from the upstream `*_ref` / `*_file` fields of http_config (e.g. httpBasicAuth.password_ref), which keep their prometheus/common meaning.
secretRef.$comment: #1560: name is a DNS-1123 subdomain (Kubernetes object name); key follows the Secret data key rule (Kubernetes IsConfigMapKey: [-._a-zA-Z0-9]+, at most 253, not '.' and not starting with '..'). The `secret` / `key` children are the Secret's coordinates, not the credential value: the field that holds a secretRef is the one on the redaction list, and it is masked whole. tests/ops/test_config_diff.py skips this definition by name for that reason.

receiverHttpUrl.title: Receiver HTTP(S) URL format
receiverHttpUrl.description: An http:// or https:// URL with a host and no whitespace or control characters. Alertmanager rejects a receiver URL without a scheme or host, or one with a leading space, and the whole Alertmanager config then fails to reload.
receiverHttpUrl.$comment: #2180: the one authored copy of this pattern, derived from Alertmanager v0.33.1 config.Load (receiver_presence_cases.json rows are asserted against it), in syntax ECMA-262, Python re and Go RE2 read alike; `not` covers Python re.search letting `$` match before a final newline.

receiverSmtpHostPort.title: Receiver SMTP host:port format
receiverSmtpHostPort.description: host:port with a numeric port; an IPv6 host is bracketed ([2001:db8::1]:25). Alertmanager rejects a smarthost without a port and the whole Alertmanager config then fails to reload.
receiverSmtpHostPort.$comment: #2180: same derivation, portable syntax and `not` as receiverHttpUrl.

httpConfig.title: HTTP Client Configuration
httpConfig.description: Optional HTTP client settings for webhook receiver (auth, TLS, proxy). See Alertmanager documentation.

basic_auth.title: Basic Authentication
basic_auth.description: HTTP basic authentication: username / username_file / username_ref (at most one) and password / password_file / password_ref (at most one).

oauth2.title: OAuth 2.0
oauth2.description: OAuth 2.0 client credentials. client_id and token_url are required.

authorization.title: Authorization Header
authorization.description: Authorization header: type (default Bearer; never basic, use basic_auth) and at most one of credentials / credentials_file / credentials_ref.

bearer_token.title: Bearer Token
bearer_token.description: HTTP Bearer token for authentication. A string: quote a token YAML would read as a number or date.

bearer_token_file.title: Bearer Token File
bearer_token_file.description: Path of a file holding the Bearer token. A string: quote a path YAML would read as a number or date.

tls_config.title: TLS Configuration
tls_config.description: TLS settings for the connection to the webhook.

follow_redirects.title: Follow Redirects
follow_redirects.description: Whether to follow HTTP 3xx redirects (Alertmanager's default: true). The route generator passes it through as written, so write a YAML boolean, not a quoted word.

enable_http2.title: Enable HTTP/2
enable_http2.description: Whether to enable HTTP/2 (Alertmanager's default: true). The route generator passes it through as written, so write a YAML boolean, not a quoted word.

http_headers.title: HTTP Headers
http_headers.description: Extra headers to send, by header name: each a mapping of values / secrets / files lists. Headers Alertmanager reserves (Authorization, Content-Type, ...) are refused.

proxy_url.title: Proxy URL
proxy_url.description: HTTP proxy URL. Alertmanager refuses the whole config when Go's net/url cannot parse it; that parser is not expressible as a pattern here. The route generator leaves it to its amtool gate (da-guard no longer judges routing, ADR-036 §9).

no_proxy.title: No Proxy
no_proxy.description: Comma-separated hosts, IPs or CIDRs that bypass proxy_url. Needs proxy_url; not together with proxy_from_environment: true.

proxy_from_environment.title: Proxy From Environment
proxy_from_environment.description: Use the proxy from HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY / NO_PROXY. Not together with a non-empty proxy_url or a no_proxy.

proxy_connect_header.title: Proxy CONNECT Headers
proxy_connect_header.description: Headers sent to the proxy on CONNECT, each a list of values. Needs a non-empty proxy_url or proxy_from_environment: true.

httpConfig.$comment: #2295 / #2984: `properties` is the http_config key set Alertmanager accepts (prometheus/common HTTPClientConfig with its inline ProxyConfig), and each nested definition (httpBasicAuth, httpAuthorization, httpOAuth2, httpTLSConfig, httpHeader) is the key set of the struct Alertmanager decodes it into; tests/alertmanager-inhibit TestSchemaHTTPConfigKeys_MatchAlertmanager pins every one of them by reflection. additionalProperties: false therefore refuses only what Alertmanager refuses (an unknown key, at any depth, fails the whole config). The route generator passes http_config through whole, and the Python check judges only its top level, so the nested rules here are the schema's and Alertmanager's alone (the rows carrying python_differs in receiver_presence_cases.json). The `allOf` pairs are every pair of basic_auth / oauth2 / authorization / bearer_token / bearer_token_file: Alertmanager (HTTPClientConfig.Validate) refuses more than one, null and an empty bearer_token / bearer_token_file count as unset, an empty mapping counts as set. The Python copy (_lib_constants.HTTP_CONFIG_AUTH_FIELDS) is pinned by tests/shared/test_receiver_spec_parity.py and the rows of receiver_presence_cases.json.

httpProxyRules.title: Alertmanager proxy rules
httpProxyRules.description: prometheus/common ProxyConfig.Validate, for http_config and for oauth2 (which inlines the same proxy keys).

type.description: Default Bearer. Alertmanager refuses basic in any case, surrounding whitespace trimmed: use basic_auth.

httpOAuth2.title: OAuth 2.0
httpOAuth2.$comment: #2984: prometheus/common HTTPClientConfig.Validate's oauth2 half: client_id and token_url non-empty; with the JWT bearer grant at most one client_certificate_key form and signature_algorithm one of RS256 / RS384 / RS512 (an unexported list there, copied by hand), otherwise at most one client_secret form. The inline ProxyConfig is validated as http_config's is. proxy_from_environment takes a real boolean here: the route generator rewrites a YAML 1.1 word only at http_config's own level.

httpTLSConfig.title: TLS Configuration
httpTLSConfig.$comment: #2984: prometheus/common TLSConfig.Validate: at most one of each of ca / cert / key in its three forms, and a client cert needs a client key and the reverse. min_version / max_version: the keys of prometheus/common TLSVersions (pinned by tests/alertmanager-inhibit).

httpHeaders.title: HTTP Headers
httpHeaders.$comment: #2984: the names prometheus/common ReservedHeaders refuses, compared after http.CanonicalHeaderKey, i.e. in any case (pinned by tests/alertmanager-inhibit).

yamlTrue.title: YAML boolean true
yamlTrue.description: The value of definitions.yamlBool that means true: the boolean true.
yamlTrue.$comment: #2984 / #2906: the true half of yamlBool; tests/shared/test_receiver_spec_parity.py pins the two together.

httpConfigOrNull.title: HTTP client configuration or null
httpConfigOrNull.description: http_config: null counts as not given, as in Alertmanager.

severityDedup.title: Severity dedup mode
severityDedup.description: 'enable' (default) or 'disable', and every other spelling the route generator and the exporter's ResolveSeverityDedup read (trimmed, any case): enable / enabled / on / true turn dedup on, disable / disabled / off / false turn it off. Also an unquoted true / false, or null (the default, enable). Any other value — `"no"`, an unquoted `no` or `yes` (strings to yaml.v3), a number — is refused, as the route generator refuses the whole tree on it.
severityDedup.$comment: #2906: the word list is _grar_parse.SEVERITY_DEDUP_*_WORDS, pinned to resolve.go's ResolveSeverityDedup by tests/shared/test_severity_dedup_vocabulary_parity.py.

yamlBool.title: YAML boolean
yamlBool.description: true / false (unquoted), or null (not given). A string is refused whatever it spells — `"true"`, and an unquoted `yes` / `no` / `on` / `off`, which yaml.v3 reads as a string — as the route generator refuses it (it reads conf.d through da-guard parse-tree and judges a boolean field by type alone, ADR-036 §2).
yamlBool.$comment: #2906: no YAML 1.1 word list any more; the route generator takes exactly this (_lib_validation.is_bool_or_unset).

routingOverride.title: Routing Override
routingOverride.description: Per-alertname or metric_group routing override. First matching override wins.

alertname.title: Alert Name
alertname.description: Alert rule name to match (e.g., 'HighConnections'). Mutually exclusive with metric_group.

metric_group.title: Metric Group
metric_group.description: Metric group to match (e.g., 'mysql_connections'). Mutually exclusive with alertname.

receiver.title: Override Receiver
receiver.description: Receiver for alerts matching this override.

routingRoute.title: Label-Match Sub-Route (ADR-007)
routingRoute.description: One sub-route under the tenant's main route. The generator renders `match` as equality matchers only (label="value"); the tenant="<id>" matcher stays on the parent route. Timing / group_by left out are inherited from the tenant's main route, and declared timing goes through the same guardrails as the main route.
routingRoute.$comment: #2245 — label equality only: no regex, no `continue`, no Alertmanager `matchers` strings. An empty `match` would shadow the main receiver for every alert of the tenant, hence minProperties 1.

match.title: Label Equality Match
match.description: Label name → exact value, all of which must be equal for the sub-route to match (e.g. {severity: critical}).

receiver.title: Sub-Route Receiver
receiver.description: Receiver for alerts matching this sub-route.

routingEnforced.title: Platform-Enforced Routing (v1.13.0+)
routingEnforced.description: Platform-level routing inserted before tenant routes. Enables dual-perspective alerts: NOC receives platform_summary, tenant receives summary. Inserted with continue: true so tenant routes also fire. See scenarios/alert-routing-split.md.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Whether to enable platform-enforced routing. Set to false or omit to disable.

receiver.title: NOC Receiver
receiver.description: Receiver for NOC (platform-perspective notifications). Usually a webhook to incident management system.

match.title: Match Conditions
match.description: List of Alertmanager matcher strings (e.g., 'severity="critical"'), rendered as the enforced route's `matchers`. An alert is routed here only when it matches ALL of them (AND, as Alertmanager reads `matchers`); for OR use one regex matcher such as 'severity=~"critical|warning"'. Omitted, null or [] = no matcher (every alert). Anything else — a mapping such as {severity: critical} (the routes[i].match spelling), a scalar, or an element that is not a string with a non-whitespace character — makes the generator render no enforced route from this block (#2989).

routingDefaults.title: Routing Defaults (v1.4.0+)
routingDefaults.description: Default routing config for tenants without explicit _routing. Supports {{tenant}} placeholder for dynamic per-tenant values. Typically set in _defaults.yaml, not per-tenant.

receiver.title: Default Receiver
receiver.description: Default receiver for tenants. Receiver fields can use {{tenant}} placeholder.

overrides.title: Default Per-Alertname/Metric-Group Overrides
overrides.description: Overrides every tenant under this level inherits unless its profile or _routing writes overrides (shallow merge; a tenant opts out with overrides: ~ or []). Same entries as the tenant's _routing.overrides. Null is not accepted here: in a subdirectory level the generator refuses it (exit 2).

routingDefaults.$comment: #2521: overrides was missing although the generator merges _routing_defaults.overrides into every tenant and cli-reference documents it. routes is deliberately NOT here: the generator drops _routing_defaults.routes before any merge with a blocking WARN, and da-guard reports routing_defaults_routes_ignored (#2245) — label-match routes belong in a routing profile or the tenant's _routing.

defaultsConfig.title: _defaults.yaml Configuration (v2.7.0 ADR-017)
defaultsConfig.description: Schema for _defaults.yaml files placed at domain, region, or environment levels in hierarchical conf.d/. Values are deep-merged into all tenant configs under that directory. Merge semantics: dict=deep merge with child override, array=replace (not concat), null=opt-out (remove inherited key). _metadata fields are skipped during merge.
defaultsConfig.$comment: A _defaults.yaml at conf.d/finance/_defaults.yaml applies to all tenants under finance/. Deeper _defaults.yaml files override shallower ones (env > region > domain).

_metadata.description: Default metadata inherited by all tenants under this directory. Individual tenant _metadata fields override these defaults.

_routing.description: Default routing configuration inherited by all tenants under this directory.

_routing_profile.description: Default routing profile for tenants under this directory.

_silent_mode.description: Default silent mode inherited by all tenants under this directory.

_severity_dedup.description: Default severity dedup mode for tenants under this directory. Same vocabulary as the tenant-level key (definitions.severityDedup).

_custom_alerts.title: Custom Alerts in a _defaults.yaml — not served (ADR-024 §3)
_custom_alerts.description: The exporter does NOT serve `_custom_alerts` declared here: there is no subtree inheritance for custom alerts (`da-guard effective` marks them not_served for tenants with no other source). The custom-alert compiler compiles what the exporter serves (#3042), so it builds no rule for them either.

customAlertList.title: Custom Alert Recipe Declarations (v2.9.0 ADR-024 Capability B)
customAlertList.description: List of custom alert recipe instances. Each fills a platform-authored recipe's parameters — the tenant never writes PromQL. The exporter takes each tenant's list from one place — its own entry, else its `tenants:` entry in a root platform file, else the bound profile — and never merges; `_custom_alerts` in a _defaults.yaml is not served (ADR-024 §3). See rule-packs/recipes/ and docs/design/config-driven.md.

customAlertInstance.title: Custom Alert Recipe Instance
customAlertInstance.description: One parameterized custom alert. The compiler groups instances by shape signature (recipe, metric, op, window, quantile, denominator, selectors) and emits ONE vectorized rule per shape.

allOf.$comment: Three-way recipe-shape branch (ADR-031 added slo_burn_rate). `threshold` moved from the instance-level required into the two non-slo branches: slo_burn_rate REPLACES it with `objective` (severity is fixed by the recipe: fast→critical, slow→warning) and FORBIDS a stray threshold; its burn windows are fixed recipe semantics so it requires no `window` either, and op is pinned to '>' (editor-guard, mirrored imperatively in shape.py/custom_alert.go).

recipe.title: Recipe Type
recipe.description: Which platform recipe to instantiate. forecast supplies `horizon` (not `window`); slo_burn_rate supplies `objective` + `denominator_metric` (neither `window` nor `threshold` — its burn windows and severities are fixed recipe semantics, ADR-031); all others supply `window`.

name.title: Alert Name (per-tenant, human-facing)
name.description: Tenant-chosen name surfaced via the `name` label (the on-call display title). Must be unique within the declaring tenant. NOT the rule identity (that is the shape slug).

metric.title: Metric Name
metric.description: Bare Prometheus metric name. Label filtering MUST use selectors/selectors_re (never inline PromQL) — the strict pattern (no colon/braces/operators) is the first line of injection defence.

denominator_metric.title: Denominator Metric (ratio / slo_burn_rate recipes)
denominator_metric.description: Denominator counter: the ratio recipe's denominator, or slo_burn_rate's TOTAL-events counter (`metric` is the BAD-events counter). Required for slo_burn_rate (ADR-031).

objective.title: SLO Objective (slo_burn_rate recipe)
objective.description: SLO target percentage in the OPEN interval (0,100), e.g. "99.9" — =100 (error budget 0 → always fires) and =0 are rejected imperatively by the Python compiler + Go preflight (this pattern is the charset gate only). "disable" is the tri-state opt-out (the declaration keeps compiling; the exporter never emits its user_threshold series). STRING-ONLY, always quote it (the #1017 quantile lesson). NOT a shape component: it never enters recipe_id or the rule text — the exporter derives the per-severity burn thresholds (14.4×(1−obj) fast / 6×(1−obj) slow for a 30d period) at resolve time and feeds them through the existing user_threshold{severity} channel, so editing the objective never re-slugs (ADR-031).

slo_period.title: SLO Budget Period (slo_burn_rate recipe)
slo_period.description: Error-budget window the burn-rate multipliers are derived from (30d→14.4/6, 28d→13.44/5.6). NOT a shape component: it only scales the exporter-computed threshold VALUES — never enters recipe_id or the rule text, so changing it never re-slugs or forks the rule (ADR-031).

min_events.title: Minimum Bad Events (slo_burn_rate recipe)
min_events.description: Low-traffic false-positive guard (ADR-031): the fast (5m) window must contain MORE THAN this many bad events for the fast-burn alert to fire (the slow tier's floor is compiler-derived as ×6 for its 30m window). A shape component: the literal is written into the rule text and enters the recipe_id slug (`minev{N}`), so a tenant writing a value different from the others forks the shape (+~12 rules). Separately, every tenant-own slo_burn_rate declaration spends 2 cap units, whatever its value — deliberate, documented in rule-packs/recipes/slo_burn_rate.yaml. NB with the default 10, a service SUSTAINED below ~2 req/min can never trip EITHER tier even at 100% errors — the slow floor (×6 over a ×6 window) is the same per-minute rate, so it does NOT cover sustained low traffic; what it adds is bursty/intermittent coverage (the 30m aggregate smooths 5m gaps). For genuinely tiny services, consciously lower min_events — best the same value for every tenant so the shape stays single.

horizon.title: Forecast Horizon (forecast recipe)
horizon.description: How far ahead to predict (predict_linear). REQUIRED for the forecast recipe; enum-bounded (enters the recipe_id slug). The platform derives lookback = max(2·horizon, 1h) from this — the tenant never sets the lookback (an expert foot-gun).

capacity_metric.title: Capacity Metric (forecast ratio mode)
capacity_metric.description: Forecast ratio mode: the denominator (e.g. total capacity). Present → predict the headroom ratio metric/capacity crossing a fractional floor in (0, 0.5) (the current-state band; >= 0.5 is rejected); absent → raw mode (predict the gauge crossing an absolute threshold).

op.title: Comparison Operator
op.description: How the computed value is compared to the threshold (ignored by absence). `==` is threshold-recipe-only (validator-enforced, #810): exact match for an integer status/error code on a raw gauge; every other recipe rejects it (float equality on a computed value is fragile; absence compares no value).

quantile.title: Quantile (p99_latency recipe)
quantile.description: Quantile in the open interval (0,1); default 0.99. STRING-ONLY, always quote it (#1017): the exact quantile TEXT enters the recipe_id slug that the Go exporter and the Python compiler compute independently — a bare YAML number is dialect-ambiguous (PyYAML 1.1 reads a dotless exponent like 95e-2 as a string, yaml.v3 as a float), silently splitting the recipe_id join and muting the alert. Quoting pins both readers to the same text. Also interpolated raw into histogram_quantile(<quantile>, …), so it stays decimal-charset (this pattern) + range validated at write + compile time — the Go preflight and the Python compiler share one decimal regex to keep their accept-set identical (a Go hex-float like 0x1p-1 that only one side accepts would wedge the CI drift gate); the (0,1) range check lives in those validators.

threshold.title: Threshold (value[:severity])
threshold.description: Threshold value with optional severity (warning|critical, default warning). Reuses the value:severity convention. For absence this is a presence flag.

selectors.title: Exact Label Filters (=)
selectors.description: label → value, compiled to exact matchers `{label="value"}`. Reserved labels (tenant/version/__name__/severity/recipe/recipe_id/name) are rejected.

selectors_re.title: Regex Label Filters (=~)
selectors_re.description: label → regex, compiled to regex matchers `{label=~"pattern"}` (anchored by Prometheus).

mode.title: Alert Mode
mode.description: page = normal routing; silent = dry-run (null/log-only receiver, wired in a later slice).

for.title: For Duration
for.description: Pending duration before firing. Enum-bounded (TRK-326): `for` is part of the recipe_id slug, so it is restricted to a small constant set to keep vectorized-rule cardinality bounded (no O(M)→O(N) blow-up). Default 1m.

group_by.title: Per-Dimension Evaluation (bounded whitelist)
group_by.description: Extra label(s) to keep in the rule's aggregation so the alert is evaluated SEPARATELY per that dimension and fires if ANY one crosses. Bounded to a whitelist to keep cardinality safe; today only `persistentvolumeclaim` — a disk-fill alert must fire per PVC, so a small full volume is not masked by a large empty one. Like `for`, it enters the recipe_id slug (instances differing in group_by compile to distinct rules). The per-tenant threshold still broadcasts to each dimension. WARNING: every metric the recipe aggregates — including a ratio's `denominator_metric` and a forecast's `capacity_metric` — MUST carry this label, or the per-dimension join yields an empty vector and the alert SILENTLY NEVER FIRES (the kubelet disk-fill metrics both carry `persistentvolumeclaim`, so the shipped example is safe). The CI scrape-config lint (#692 P0 ③ guard) enforces this, since the compiler cannot see live label sets.
